title: Second-Order Derangement Convergence Rate
description: Refines the derangement convergence rate to a two-term asymptotic: D(n)/n! = 1/e + (-1)^n/(n+1)! + O(1/(n+2)!). Proves the second-order bound, a matching lower bound showing tightness, the error ratio formula, and sign characterization of the correction term.

meta.author: Montmort (1708), Euler (1751), formalized in Lean 4

mathlibDependencies.description: numDerangements and derangement counting for finite types
summable_pow_div_factorial for convergence of factorial series
tsum, HasSum, Summable for infinite series manipulation

originalContributions: Tail splitting lemma for the alternating factorial series
Sign characterization of the correction term for even and odd n

overview.historicalContext:
The derangement ratio D(n)/n! = ∑_{k=0}^n (-1)^k/k! converges to 1/e, as established by Montmort (1708) and Euler (1751). The first-order convergence rate |D(n)/n! - 1/e| ≤ 1/(n+1)! was formalized in DerangementsOQ03. This entry refines that to a two-term asymptotic expansion, capturing the leading correction term and proving the bound is tight.

The expansion D(n)/n! = 1/e + (-1)^n/(n+1)! + O(1/(n+2)!) is a classical result from the theory of alternating series. Each additional term of the Taylor series for e^{-1} provides one more order of accuracy, with the error bounded by the next omitted term. This is a direct consequence of the Leibniz alternating series estimation theorem applied to e^{-1} = ∑ (-1)^k/k!.
overview.problemStatement:
Prove the second-order derangement convergence rate:

|D(n)/n! - e^{-1} - (-1)^n/(n+1)!| ≤ 1/(n+2)!

This refines the first-order bound |D(n)/n! - e^{-1}| ≤ 1/(n+1)! by identifying the leading correction term as (-1)^n/(n+1)! and showing the residual is bounded by 1/(n+2)!.
overview.text:
A 243-line formalization proving the second-order asymptotic expansion for the derangement ratio D(n)/n!. Building on the DerangementsOQ03 convergence rate infrastructure, the main theorem `second_order_convergence_rate` establishes:

|D(n)/n! - e^{-1} - (-1)^n/(n+1)!| ≤ 1/(n+2)!

The proof splits the tail of the alternating factorial series at one additional term, then applies the existing alternating series bound to the residual. A matching lower bound `second_order_lower_bound` shows the first-order error is at least 1/(n+1)! - 1/(n+2)!, proving tightness. The error ratio formula shows each step improves by a factor of 1/(n+2), and sign theorems characterize the correction term's alternating behavior.
overview.proofStrategy:
The proof proceeds by refining the tail decomposition from DerangementsOQ03:

1. **Tail splitting**: Show ∑' k, f(m+k) = f(m) + ∑' k, f(m+1+k) for summable series, via `tsum_eq_zero_add` applied to the shifted series.

2. **Second-order bound**: Starting from D(n)/n! - e^{-1} = -(∑' k, altFactTerm(n+1+k)), split off the first tail term:
   - ∑' k, altFactTerm(n+1+k) = altFactTerm(n+1) + ∑' k, altFactTerm(n+2+k)
   - Since altFactTerm(n+1) = (-1)^{n+1}/(n+1)!, the term -altFactTerm(n+1) = (-1)^n/(n+1)! cancels with the correction
   - The residual -(∑' k, altFactTerm(n+2+k)) has |·| ≤ 1/(n+2)! by the existing alternating_tail_bound

3. **Lower bound**: By the reverse triangle inequality, |correction + residual| ≥ |correction| - |residual|, giving the lower bound 1/(n+1)! - 1/(n+2)!.

4. **Error ratio**: Direct computation: (n+2)! = (n+1)! · (n+2), so 1/(n+2)! = 1/(n+1)! · 1/(n+2).
keyInsights: **One more term of the alternating series**: The second-order bound follows by splitting off one additional term from the tail. The existing alternating_tail_bound at the shifted index provides the residual estimate. This is the general pattern: each additional term gives one more order of accuracy.

**Tightness via reverse triangle inequality**: The lower bound 1/(n+1)! - 1/(n+2)! shows the first-order error bound 1/(n+1)! is essentially tight — the actual error is within a factor of (1 - 1/(n+2)) of the bound.

**Geometric decay**: The error ratio 1/(n+2) shows super-exponential convergence — each additional permutation element reduces the approximation error by a factor of roughly 1/n. This is much faster than geometric convergence.

**Sign alternation captured**: The correction term (-1)^n/(n+1)! precisely captures the alternating overshoot/undershoot pattern: even n gives D(n)/n! > 1/e, odd n gives D(n)/n! < 1/e, with the signed magnitude ≈ 1/(n+1)!.

**General pattern for asymptotic expansions**: The tail splitting technique applied here is the formal backbone for a general theorem: splitting off k terms from the tail of any alternating series gives a k-term asymptotic expansion with residual bounded by the (k+1)-th term. The Lean implementation uses `tsum_eq_zero_add` with shifted indexing to peel off one term at a time. This gives an algorithmic procedure: to get k-th order accuracy, apply `tsum_tail_split` k times, each time recording the leading term and passing the shifted tail to the existing bound.

sections.title: Tail Splitting Lemma
sections.summary: Proves that the tail of the alternating factorial series can be split: ∑' k, f(m+k) = f(m) + ∑' k, f(m+1+k).

sections.title: Second-Order Convergence Rate
sections.summary: Main theorem: |D(n)/n! - e^{-1} - (-1)^n/(n+1)!| ≤ 1/(n+2)!. Splits the tail at one more term and applies the alternating bound to the residual.

sections.title: Lower Bound (Tightness)
sections.summary: Proves 1/(n+1)! - 1/(n+2)! ≤ |D(n)/n! - e^{-1}|, showing the first-order error bound is tight.

sections.title: Error Ratio
sections.summary: The error bound improves by factor 1/(n+2) per step: 1/(n+2)! = 1/(n+1)! · 1/(n+2).

sections.title: Correction Term Sign
sections.summary: The correction term (-1)^n/(n+1)! is positive for even n (overshoot) and negative for odd n (undershoot).

sections.title: Concrete Bounds
sections.summary: Second-order error bounds for n = 0 (≤ 1/2), n = 1 (≤ 1/6), and n = 2 (≤ 1/24).

crossReferences.description: Directly extends the first-order convergence rate |D(n)/n! - 1/e| ≤ 1/(n+1)! to the two-term asymptotic, adding the leading correction term (-1)^n/(n+1)! and a tighter residual bound.
Depends on the derangement counting formula D(n) = n! · ∑_{k=0}^n (-1)^k/k! and the connection to the Taylor series of e^{-1}.

conclusion.summary: A complete formalization of the second-order derangement convergence rate: D(n)/n! = 1/e + (-1)^n/(n+1)! + O(1/(n+2)!). The main theorem establishes the two-term asymptotic with a matching lower bound proving tightness, error ratio formula showing super-exponential convergence, and sign characterization of the correction term. All 9 theorems are fully proved with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications:
**1. Practical Accuracy**: The two-term approximation D(n)/n! ≈ 1/e + (-1)^n/(n+1)! gives dramatically better accuracy than the simple 1/e approximation. For n = 5, the error drops from 1/720 to 1/5040.

**2. Pattern for Higher-Order Expansions**: The tail splitting technique generalizes: splitting off k terms gives a k-term asymptotic expansion with residual O(1/(n+k+1)!). This is the general structure of asymptotic series.

**3. Complete Error Analysis**: The combination of upper and lower bounds pinpoints the error to within a factor of 1/(n+2) of the leading term, giving a complete characterization of the approximation quality.
openQuestions: Can the k-term asymptotic expansion be formalized for arbitrary k, giving |D(n)/n! - ∑_{j=0}^{k} (-1)^{n+j+1}/(n+j+1)!| ≤ 1/(n+k+2)!?
Can the exact error D(n)/n! - 1/e be expressed as a closed-form alternating sum with the sign determined by the parity of n?
